chunks: Muhammad ibn Ya'qub from Ali from his father from Safwan ibn Yahya from Isḥaq ibn 'Ammar from Abu 'Abdillah (peace be upon him)

He (peace be upon him) said: 'If the owner of Dhihar is unable to pay the expiation, let him seek forgiveness from his Lord and intend not to return [to the act] before he consummates [the marriage], then let him consummate, and that will suffice for him in place of the expiation. When he finds the means to pay what expiates it, on any of the days, let him pay it. And if he gives charity from his hand, or feeds himself and his family, that will suffice for him if he is needy. And if he does not find that, let him seek forgiveness from his Lord and intend not to return; that is sufficient for him, and God is the Expiator.'

key_terms.الظِّهَار: Dhihar (a specific form of divorce/oath in Islamic jurisprudence)

ai.seo_question: What is the expiation for Dhihar if the husband cannot afford it?
ai.summary: Shaykh al-Tusi records this ruling in *Tahdhib al-Ahkam*, highlighting the juristic flexibility for those unable to pay the three-month fast or feed sixty poor people mandated by Surah al-Mujadila. The hadith establishes a tiered approach: immediate consumption with sincere repentance serves as a provisional substitute, while voluntary charity or self-feeding acts as a valid interim expiation for the needy until full capacity is restored. This reflects the Shia emphasis on ease (*taysir*) in applying divine laws to varying economic conditions.
